g.text: The parlour operates in 30-minute time slots. Each slot is generated dynamically based on
branch opening hours and service duration. The system never hard-codes slots in the database
Last appointment must END by 8 PM
Users cannot book more than 2 months in advance
Cannot book a slot starting within 2 hours
User can cancel up to 2 hours before the appointment
9.2 Slot Availability Logic — Step by Step
When a user selects a service and a date, the system runs this process to determine which
• Calculate all possible slots for the day: 09:00, 09:30, 10:00 ... 19:30 (last slot for a
• Filter slots that are in the past or within the 2-hour minimum advance window.
• Query Bookings table: find all CONFIRMED or PENDING bookings for the selected date,
branch, and staff (if staff is selected).
• For each booked slot, mark the time range as UNAVAILABLE (including service duration — a
• If staff_id is provided: only check that staff member's bookings. If no staff selected:
check parlour-level capacity (total staff available for that slot).
• Return remaining AVAILABLE slots to the user as a visual grid.
✅ Example: User wants a Facial (60 min) on Saturday. Slots 10:00 and 11:00 are already
booked by two different customers. So the 10:00 slot appears RED (unavailable). But 11:30 is
User selects a specific staff member
System checks ONLY that staff member's availability. If she's busy, that slot shows as
System finds all staff qualified for the service and checks if at least one is free in the
System assigns the staff member with fewest bookings that day (load balancing). Stored in
Admin marks staff as unavailable. System reassigns all their future bookings to another
Only staff with the service in their specializations array appear as options for that
Immediately after user submits booking (awaiting payment)
When customer arrives and admin checks them in
After service is done, marked by admin or staff
By user (2 hrs before) or by admin anytime
User did not show up, admin marks after appointment time
A race condition occurs when two users try to book the same slot at exactly the same time.
The system prevents double-booking using database-level locking.
• Step 1: When a booking is submitted, the API starts a database transaction.
• Step 2: It does a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the relevant time slot row — this locks it.
• Step 3: If another request tries to book the same slot simultaneously, it waits.
• Step 4: First request succeeds → booking created → lock released.
• Step 5: Second request runs → sees slot is now taken → returns 409 Conflict.
• Step 6: User who lost the race gets: 'माफ़ करें, यह स्लॉट अभी भर गया। कोई दूसरा समय
⚠️ Edge Case: User holds a slot in the booking form for 10 minutes without completing
payment. System should hold a PENDING booking for maximum 15 minutes, then auto-expire it,
releasing the slot back to available.
